_comment: FROZEN ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. This file is the scientific instrument in
CI: a numerical criterion that can say no before any human reads a
diff. In a reference project the same wrong algorithm was pushed three
times in different forms and a frozen acceptance number rejected it
three times.
Every value here was MEASURED by mirror/geomap_mirror/references.py on
13-Aug-2026 (pyproj 3.7.2 / PROJ 9.5.1). None was copied from a
document. Four values in handover revision 2.0 were refuted by that
run and do not appear here; see RECORDS.md R-002.
A tolerance is NEVER widened to make a run pass. If a value drifts,
that is a finding: decompose the residual first. A criterion loosened
until green is an instrument destroyed in place.
'source' records where the authority comes from, so the next reader
does not have to guess whether a number is published, measured or
analytic.

mercator_y_at_lat35.source: analytic: ln(tan(45 + 17.5 deg)); confirmed against O1 and O4

lcc_x_at_35N_75W.source: O1 Snyder 1987 p.296 worked example, spherical, R=1

lcc_y_at_35N_75W.source: O1 Snyder 1987 p.296 worked example, spherical, R=1

lcc_33_45_cone_constant.source: analytic, SPHERICAL. The handover quoted 0.6304962, which is the ELLIPSOIDAL Clarke-1866 value (matches to 2.6e-7) for a model geoMap does not use. Finding PV-011.

polarstereo_rho_lat70_sp71.source: analytic (1+sin 71)*tan(10 deg), confirmed by O4 to 1e-10. The handover quoted 0.6116372, which matches no evaluation of any formula in either model. Finding PV-002.

robinson_X_at_lat50.source: O2 Robinson table node. The handover quoted 0.9427, which is the X entry at lat 35. Finding PV-005.

robinson_Y_at_lat50.source: O2 Robinson table node. The handover quoted 0.5722, which is the X entry at lat 85. Finding PV-005.

robinson_pchip_node_reproduction.source: PCHIP must reproduce its own table nodes exactly; anything looser hides an interpolation defect

hammer_x_limit_at_equator.source: analytic limit 2*sqrt(2) as lon -> 180 at the equator

paris_nyc_spherical_km.source: haversine at the authalic radius; the WGS84 geodesic is 5852.9 km (O4), a difference of -0.268%, which is what decision D-001's '<= 0.3%' claim rests on

invariants_max._comment: Upper bounds on measured errors. Analytic invariants (O3): equal-area projections have AreaScale 1, conformal ones have h == k, a conic has k == 1 on both standard parallels, Mercator has k == sec(phi). Bounds sit about a decade above the measured values, so drift is visible before it is harmful.

equal_area_max_relative_error._comment: Global quad integral against 4*pi, 1-degree quads. Pseudocylindricals only: the azimuthal rim and the conic apex are singular, so a global integral there measures discretisation rather than the projection (finding PV-007).

round_trip_max_deg_error._comment: Forward then inverse, 10000 quasi-random in-domain points, seed 42. Lambert azimuthal is inherently worse: asin conditioning at the antipodal rim (PV-010). Everything else is double-precision closed form or a converged iteration.

proj_max_abs_diff._comment: Agreement with the independent oracle O4 in projected units (Earth radii). Robinson is excluded from tight agreement: PROJ uses its own interpolation of the Robinson table, so it certifies only to about 1e-3 there (mirror limit L5). That is corroboration, not a tolerance.

_comment: Boolean criteria pinning the v1 defects this redesign exists to fix.
Added after a fault-injection run showed the gate caught a reinstated
Robinson wrap bug ONLY through oracle disagreement on two OTHER
projections: Robinson's own round trip stayed self-consistent while
being wrong. That is failure mode F1 - no self-consistency check can
catch a consistently wrong program - and it is why each defect needs
its own pinned criterion rather than trusting a general suite.

robinson_x_at_lon359.meaning: F2: project(359,10,robinson) must be negative and |x|<0.02. v1 returned about +3.0 because it passed an unwrapped longitude difference to the table.

mercator_y_at_lat87_is_nan.meaning: F3: latitudes outside crs.Domain.LatLimit return NaN. v1 clamped to +/-85 and drew the data at the wrong place.

_comment: Added by Stage 0.3, when oracle rows O7 and O8 were filled. Each is
an upper bound on a MEASURED quantity, set about a decade above what
the run reads, so drift is visible before it is harmful.
The path is dotted: a key 'a.b.c' reads values['a']['b']['c'].
regrid_mass_closure_floor.measured discharges handover debt V7. The
handover guessed 1e-12; the measured floor at 2161x4321 -> 181x361,
over the worst of three summation orders, is 2.15e-14. TolMass is
set one decade above that, at 1e-13 - which is TIGHTER than the
guess, not looser.
hillshade_vs_O8_gdal.hillshade_max_abs_error_dn is bounded at 0, not
at 1: the mirror reproduces gdaldem's uint8 output EXACTLY over the
compared interior. Bounding it at the quantisation step would have
thrown away a decade of evidence that was actually there.
Boolean criteria. 'discriminates' is the one that matters: it
asserts the analytic regrid check has been SEEN to reject a wrong
algorithm (latitude weighted in degrees rather than in sin lat), not
merely to accept the right one. A check never seen to fail is not
evidence (BEST_PRACTICE 5.8).
